quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
Traffic signal ahead.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When should you drive on the shoulder to pass a car?

options.text: If the vehicle ahead of you is turning left.
Never.
If the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never pass a car on the shoulder. The other driver will not expect you there and may pull onto the road without seeing you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No passing zone.
Slow-moving vehicle.
Two-way traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: A yellow triangular sign with black letters means no passing zone. You will see it on the left side of a two-lane road where passing is not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign tell you about the road ahead?

options.text: Turns sharply right, then left.
Curves right, then left.
Curves right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road curves to the right, then to the left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to stop.
You must come to a complete stop.
Stop only if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: The stop sign is the only eight-sided sign on the road. You must come to a complete stop and wait until it is safe before going through the intersection.

questions.question: What should a driver do about the right-of-way?

options.text: Assume all drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you always have the right-of-way. Be ready to yield if it helps avoid a crash.

questions.question: What does this sign warn about?

options.text: Railroad crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: Round signs with black markings warn you about railroad crossings ahead. Yellow warning signs tell you about other hazards.

questions.question: When can you drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly in both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never drive around or under a lowered gate. Wait until the gate is raised and you can see clearly in both directions before crossing.

questions.question: When should you sound your horn while passing another car?

options.text: If the car is turning into your lane.
If the car is driving very slowly.
If the car is signaling a right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the car is turning into your lane.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn a driver who does not see you and is about to turn into your lane.

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?

options.text: There is a steep hill ahead.
No trucks are allowed on the upcoming hill.
A logging road is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This yellow sign warns you about a steep hill. Slow down and control your speed to protect your brakes.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells you that traffic from the right may merge. Be ready to let traffic merge safely.

questions.question: Is it ever okay to drive if medication affects your driving?

options.text: No, never.
Yes, if you don't feel drowsy.
Yes, if a doctor prescribed it.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: You cannot drive if any substance affects your ability to drive safely. This includes alcohol, prescription drugs, over-the-counter drugs, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: When entering the interstate, you should check for a gap, match the traffic speed, signal, and then:

options.text: Expect other cars to let you in since you have the right-of-way.
Merge carefully into the gap.
Wait for the lane to completely clear before merging.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge carefully into the gap.
questions.explanation: Find a gap in traffic, speed up to match the other cars, and signal. Then merge safely into the gap. Watch other traffic and do not expect them to make room for you.

questions.question: After passing a car on the left, when is it safe to move back to the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the car over your right shoulder.
When you can see the front of the car in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You can move back to the right lane when you see the headlights of the car you passed in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: How do sudden wind gusts affect highway driving?

options.text: They only affect large vehicles.
They only cause visibility problems.
They can cause problems for all vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can cause problems for all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong wind can affect all drivers. It can blow dirt and dust into the road, reducing visibility. Wind can also physically push your vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Cars on the right go first.
You have the right-of-way.
Let other traffic pass before you go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other traffic pass before you go.
questions.explanation: This sign means you must yield. Slow down and let cars and pedestrians cross before you proceed. Stop if needed.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines mean?

options.text: No one can pass.
Both sides can pass.
Only the right lane can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one can pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop only if other cars are coming.
Yield to pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that bicycles may be crossing the road.

questions.question: What happens if you drive slower than other traffic?

options.text: You may block traffic and get a ticket.
You improve traffic flow.
You show good defensive driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may block traffic and get a ticket.
questions.explanation: Drive slowly in heavy traffic or bad weather. But if you drive too slowly and block normal traffic movement, you can get a ticket. Match the speed of traffic unless the traffic is speeding.

questions.question: You want to pass a pedestrian on the road, but a car is coming toward you. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and let the car pass first, then pass the pedestrian.
Keep driving at the same speed. The other car must stop for you.
Honk your horn to make the pedestrian move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the car pass first, then pass the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. If you want to pass a pedestrian but a car is coming, slow down and let the car pass. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

questions.question: To turn quickly, where should your hands be on the steering wheel?

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other at the top of the steering wheel.
One at the top and one at the bottom of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position is comfortable and helps you turn safely at high speeds.

questions.question: When merging onto an interstate highway, what should you do?

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into the traffic lane.
Merge across two lanes at the same time.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: Find a gap large enough for you to safely enter traffic. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there are no safe gaps to merge into.

questions.question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, what should you do?

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch your lights to high beams.
Turn your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Look at the right edge of the road instead of straight ahead. This keeps your vehicle on the road safely until you pass the oncoming vehicle.

questions.question: What are blind spots?

options.text: Areas in your vision when you become tired.
Areas of the road that you cannot see in your mirrors.
Traffic control devices.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas of the road that you cannot see in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. Check the areas near the rear corners of your vehicle. These areas are called blind spots because your mirrors cannot show them.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign shows a crosswalk, whether it is marked on the pavement or not. When you see this sign, be alert and let pedestrians cross safely.

questions.question: Traffic is merging into your lane on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Make room for the merging traffic if you safely can.
Drive faster to keep your right-of-way.
Always keep your position and do not move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for the merging traffic if you safely can.
questions.explanation: When you can do so safely, make room to let vehicles merge into your lane.

questions.question: What does a red painted curb mean?

options.text: Loading zone.
The area is for picking up or dropping off passengers.
No parking, standing, or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking, standing, or stopping.
questions.explanation: You cannot stop, stand, or park at a red-painted curb.

questions.question: Which factor affects how quickly someone absorbs alcohol?

options.text: Weight
Height
Intelligence

questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: A person's weight, biological sex, how much food is in their stomach, and the number of drinks they have had all affect alcohol absorption. The only way to remove alcohol from your system is to wait.

questions.question: What does a blood alcohol concentration of 0.02 percent do?

options.text: It will not affect your driving.
It will not put other drivers at risk.
It will double your chances of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: It will double your chances of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Each increase of 0.02 percent in blood alcohol concentration nearly doubles your risk of a fatal crash.

questions.question: Which of these is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using high beam lights in fog.
Staring straight ahead at the road.
Checking your rearview mirrors regularly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your rearview mirrors regularly.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors every two to five seconds to watch for hazards. Do not stare only at the road ahead—it is dangerous. In fog, use low beam headlights, not high beams.
